To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the benefit from Bagged/Boosted J4. 8 decision trees does not always increase monotonically along with the increase in the training set size and the benefit from unpruned decision tree ensemble is usually larger than that from pruned decision tree ensemble.

the benefits from ensemble are usually positively correlated with the sizes of training sets, that the benefit from Boosted unpruned decision tree ensembles usually is bigger than that from Boosted pruned decision tree ensem- bles, and that the benefit from Bagged unpruned decision-tree ensembles usually is smaller than that from Bagged pruned decision-tree en- sembles.

the benefit from Bagged J4.8 is usually not significantly impacted by the training set size, while the benefit from Boosted J4.8 is usually increased by enlarging the training size, but this increase is not consistent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the training set sizes on the benefit from Bagged/ Boosting decision trees and the relationship between pruning and the benefit.
the benefit from ensemble and its relationship to the size of the data set.
the relationship between the size of the given training set and the benefit from ensembling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of training set size on the benefit from Bagged/ Boosting J4.8 is not monotonic.
the benefit from ensembles is usually more significant for larger training sets, but the increase of the size of training set does not necessarily lead to the increase of the benefit from ensembling.

, the benefit from Bagged decision trees is usually insensitive to the size of the original training set and that, the benefit of Boosted decision trees tends to increase along with the increase in the size of the initial training set but may not always be the case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the size of training set should not be increased blindly for ensemble learning.
, for the purpose of ensemble learning, a small size of the training data is sufficient, and that the benefit from ensembles of unpruned trees may be bigger than that from ensembles of pruned trees.
the benefit from Boosted/Bagged decision trees is not always positively correlated to the size of the available training set.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the benefit from Boosted J4 decision trees may be more significant than that from Bagged J4 decision trees, which is contrary to the common belief that the benefit from Bagged decision trees is usually greater than that from Boosted decision trees.
the training set size should be carefully considered when designing ensemble methods.
the benefit from ensembles may not always increase with the increase of training set size and it is usually bigger for unpruned decision tree ensembles than for pruned ones.
